findings.explanation: HOL4's CHR is the ABS function of the char type definition. It is specified only by char_BIJ: CHR (ORD a) = a, and n < 256 <=> ORD (CHR n) = n. Saved theorems (CHR_11, ORD_CHR_RWT, CHR_ONTO, ...) leave CHR n open for n >= 256, apart from ORD (CHR n) <> n; ORD_CHR_COMPUTE gives only a FAIL term there. The Lean definition is transparent and returns the character 0 for every n >= 256, so Lean proves CHR 256 = CHR 0, ORD (CHR 256) = 0 and CHR 256 = CHR 257, none of which HOL4 decides.
findings.repair:
opaque CHR_unspec : Nat → char
def CHR (n : Nat) : char := if h : n < 256 then ⟨n, h⟩ else CHR_unspec n
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.String

example : HOL.CHR 256 = HOL.CHR 0 := by
  first
    | rfl
    | simp [HOL.CHR]

example : HOL.ORD (HOL.CHR 256) = 0 := by
  first
    | rfl
    | simp [HOL.CHR, HOL.ORD]
